answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, time-weighted stake before it can influence trades, and its weight grows only as that stake survives across the horizon. A wharf operator can require counterparties to settle through escrow, then slash the lock when an agent defaults or is proven to collude. An attacker can still forge many identities, but each needs separate capital held at risk for long enough to earn influence; splitting one stake among aliases gains no extra weight.
